The sentence expresses a scheduled meeting. The noun לִבֵּית־הַנְּדִירוֹן ('the committee') is constructed with the Hebrew definite article לְ- + בֵּית + characteristic noun הַנְּדִירוֹן (derived from נְדְוֵ׳וּ, meaning 'one who decides'—a decision-maker). This is Hebrew's way of forming institutional nouns. The verb יוֹנְדָאגַאוִין is Algonquian 'to come together, to gather,' with future prefix יַ- and the time adverb בַּמָּרָתָא following. The possessive prefix יוֹ- ('its own way of gathering') turns the verb into a noun-like form: 'its coming-together.'

The time phrase בַּמָּרָתָא יוֹנְדָאגוֵ׳ין is fully Algonquian: בַּ- (in/at) + מָּרָתָא (day/time) + יוֹנְדָאגוֵ׳ין (Tuesday, literally 'gathering day'). Hebrew provides the institution; Algonquian provides the calendar.
